Peters voted for the Laken Riley Act in January 2025 as one of 12 Senate Democrats, mandating detention of undocumented immigrants convicted of certain crimes, while also supporting DACA and pathways to legal status for long-term residents -- consistent with prioritizing deportation of recent border crossers while allowing long-term residents to seek legal status.

Peters has opposed offshore drilling and backed renewable energy investment while not calling for an outright ban on new fossil fuel permits; his record reflects maintaining current production levels within existing environmental regulations rather than expansion or an immediate ban.

Peters voted for the ACA and explicitly supports a Medicare public option alongside private insurance, while opposing full privatization or single-payer; he backed extending ACA enhanced tax credits in 2025.

Peters has sponsored federal funding for redevelopment of abandoned and foreclosed properties and supported bipartisan affordable housing investment, consistent with building affordable housing units and expanding rental assistance programs.

Peters supports DACA protections and a pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants; while he voted for the Laken Riley Act enforcement provisions, his overall record reflects significantly expanding legal immigration and creating citizenship pathways.

Peters has championed reducing recidivism and mass incarceration, co-authored data-driven crime cooperation bills, and backed criminal justice reform approaches, reflecting support for alternatives to incarceration over purely punitive responses.

Peters opposes raising the Medicare eligibility age or privatization, backed the Social Security Fairness Act in 2024, and supports lowering drug costs and expanding Medicaid; rated 98% by the Americans Retired Association for his pro-Trust Fund positions.

Peters supported the For the People Act which included independent redistricting commission provisions with equal party representation, consistent with independent commissions rather than partisan legislative control.

Peters voted Yea on the Respect for Marriage Act in November 2022 (Senate vote 362), which repeals DOMA and requires all states to recognize same-sex marriages with full federal benefits -- the strongest available congressional action for nationwide marriage equality.

Peters explicitly opposes school vouchers and supports public school funding and student loan subsidies, consistent with fully funding public schools and eliminating voucher programs that divert taxpayer money to private institutions.

Peters is rated 98% pro-Trust Fund by the Americans Retired Association, calls Social Security one of the most successful programs in our history, and strongly opposes both privatization and raising the retirement age -- consistent with expanding benefits significantly and removing the payroll tax income cap.

Peters opposes free trade deals harming Michigan workers and supports targeted tariffs against currency manipulation, but backed USMCA and the Ex-Im Bank and pressed the Trump administration on its blanket tariff approach in 2025 -- indicating selective use of tariffs to protect key industries rather than universally high tariffs.

Peters proposes a minimum 30% tax rate for those earning over $1 million and criticizes the unfair burden on the middle class, supporting modest increases on high earners while maintaining rates for middle-class families.

Peters voted Nay on S.9 in the 119th Congress (vote 100), which would have required biological sex at birth for Title IX compliance in school sports, indicating support for transgender athletes competing consistent with their gender identity.

Peters voted Yea on Senate Amendment 299 (119th Congress, vote 76) expressing continued U.S. support for Ukraine against Russian aggression; as Homeland Security Committee chairman he oversaw aid implementation and supports ongoing military and economic assistance.

Peters champions automatic voter registration, expanded early voting periods, and mail-in voting access, and supported the For the People Act -- consistent with expanding early voting and making mail-in voting available to all voters without requiring an excuse.
